title: Classic Pumpkin Pie
subtitle: smooth, gently spiced custard pie with maple whipped cream
imageAlt: A classic pumpkin pie with a slice cut out and served on a cream plate with whipped cream, beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: one 23 cm (9 in) deep pie, 8 slices

beforeYouStart.text: Use pure pumpkin purée, not pumpkin pie filling (that one is already sweetened and spiced).
Bake it the day before: it needs 2 hours to cool and set.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) with a rack in the lower third. Set the frozen shell on a baking sheet.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Whisk the pumpkin, brown sugar, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves and salt, then whisk in the eggs and evaporated milk until smooth.

steps.title: Bake hot
steps.text: Pour into the shell and bake 15 minutes.

steps.title: Bake low
steps.text: Lower to 175°C (350°F) and bake 35–45 minutes more, until the edges are set, the centre jiggles slightly and a knife near the centre comes out clean (about 80°C / 175°F).

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack at least 2 hours, then refrigerate.

fixIt.fix: It baked a little long; cover the crack with whipped cream and take it out at a slight jiggle next time.
Cover the edge with a foil ring after 25 minutes.
Bake on the lower rack on a hot baking sheet.

saleTip: Canned pumpkin sells out before Thanksgiving; buy two cans in September.
swap: 2½ tsp of our Pumpkin Pie Spice for the five spices. Homemade crust if you have one.
leftovers: Keep slices covered in the fridge; they're good cold for breakfast.
doneness: Bake until a knife near the centre comes out clean, about 80°C (175°F); the eggs are fully cooked. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooling.
source: Based on the classic evaporated-milk pumpkin pie (Libby's, Canadian Living): two-temperature bake, 220°C then 175°C.
prepAhead: Bake up to 2 days ahead and keep covered in the fridge.
reheat: Served cold or at room temperature; no reheating needed.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the ginger and cloves.

fancy.note: Maple whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon.

addSteps.title: Maple cream
addSteps.text: Whip the cream with the maple syrup to soft peaks and spoon onto each slice.

plating: Cut with a hot, wiped knife for clean slices.
A big swirl of maple cream.

why.0-9: Evaporated milk gives a dense, silky custard that sets cleanly.
why.0-1: Pure purée lets us control the sugar and spice.

funFact: Morton, Illinois, calls itself the pumpkin capital of the world; most canned pumpkin comes from there.

keeps.note: wrap well; the texture softens slightly
keeps.thaw: Thaw overnight in the fridge and serve cold

drink: Coffee or a cup of chai tea.
pairs: our pumpkin pie spice works here
